arguments.summary: Initial low-severity policy violation alert for off-hours access by user d.chen to \\10.0.8.100\shared\quarterly_reports evolved into a confirmed incident after correlation revealed lateral movement and reconnaissance activity. Investigation identified that IP 10.0.8.100 is incorrectly referenced; the actual asset involved is WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15), a low-criticality Ubuntu host managed by the helpdesk team. Multiple systems, including 10.0.3.22 and 10.0.8.100, logged network scans (Nmap SYN) targeting WS-IT-101 on 2026-04-08T14:22:10Z. User d.chen (10.0.3.22) accessed the file share during a period of elevated activity, though UEBA scoring remained low (0.35). No malicious payloads, command-and-control traffic, or data exfiltration were observed. The incident is assessed as low risk with no evidence of compromise.

arguments.summary: A data exfiltration incident was detected originating from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42), attributed to user CORP\jsmith in the Finance department. The compromise began with a phishing email triggering an encoded PowerShell command from Outlook, leading to the execution of a Cobalt Strike beacon via rundll32.exe from the Temp directory. The attacker established C2 communication over HTTPS (198.51.100.23) and performed DNS tunneling (c2.evil-example.com) for data exfiltration. Lateral movement attempts were observed via SMB to file server 10.0.5.50. Sensitive PII and financial data were exfiltrated from host WS-IT-101 (10.0.7.50) via DNS tunneling. The initial detection was delayed due to lack of correlation between DNS anomaly and endpoint process behavior.

timeline.description: User CORP\jsmith launched Outlook on WS-FIN-042.
Encoded PowerShell command executed from Outlook process.
rundll32.exe loaded malicious beacon.dll from Temp directory.
IDS alerted on Cobalt Strike C2 beacon to 198.51.100.23 over TCP/443.
Failed Kerberos TGT request from WS-FIN-042, indicating credential access attempt.
SMB access to file server 10.0.5.50, indicating lateral movement.
DLP alert triggered on data exfiltration from 10.0.7.50 to 10.0.5.14 via DNS TXT queries to c2.evil-example.com.

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_Dll_From_Temp {
    meta:
        description = "Detects unsigned DLLs loaded from Temp by rundll32"
        author = "SOC_Team"
        reference = "MITRE ATT&CK T1218.011"
        tlp = "amber"
    strings:
        $temp_path = "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" wide ascii
        $rundll_load = "rundll32.exe" wide ascii
    condition:
        $temp_path and $rundll_load and not pe.signed()}
